proof:
# The full-target midpoint-density centroid bridge fails on actual fibers

The sharp unequal midpoint density bound does not justify replacing
the original three-fiber source by the centroid of B+L eta with
L=(a+c)/a. An exact compatible interval example defeats both the
proposed source-cost inequality and the resulting actual candidate.
A Cartesian-product example does so in continuous dimension two.
All fibers have positive full volume and all three masses are
strictly below half the total. Neither example defeats OC.

The endpoint-centroid midpoint bound and its equal-endpoint corollary
already appear in additive-midpoint-chord-certificates.md. The sharp
unequal midpoint density capacity is already proved in
candidate 8b5d53df129b0528, Section 1.
The new issue here is the proposed full-target centroid bridge.

## 1. The proposed bridge and an actual family

Let A,B,C occur at integer bases -1,0,1, with volumes a,b,c and
(A+C)/2 subset B. For a<=c define

    s_d=((a^(1/d)+c^(1/d))/2)^d.

The archived coupling theorem produces a probability coupling of
the uniform endpoint laws whose midpoint law has density at most
1/s_d. Multiplying by a gives eta, with mass a and eta<=a/s_d.
One proposed extension takes

    L=(a+c)/a,
    g=centroid(1_B dx+L eta),                          (1)

and seeks, for every halfspace H through g,

    |B intersect H|+eta(H) >= Gamma_d(a+b+c)/2,        (2)

under b>=s_d and |b-c|<a. If (2) held, the usual affine midpoint
indicator inequality would make g an OC candidate for the original
three fibers. Both this inequality and that candidate can fail.

For 0<a<1, let Q=[0,1]^(d-1), with Q a point of mass one if d=1.
Put k=(3-a)/4 and define

    A=[k-a/2,k+a/2] x Q,
    B=[0,1] x Q,
    C=[k-1/2,k+1/2] x Q.                              (3)

The volumes are a,1,1. Their actual midpoint is

    D=(A+C)/2=[(1-a)/2,1] x Q,
    s=|D|=(1+a)/2.                                   (4)

Thus D is contained in B. The convex hull of these three lifted
fibers is a full-dimensional convex body in R x R^d with exactly
the specified integer fibers. The endpoints are extreme base
fibers; every convex combination at base zero is a mixture of B
and endpoint midpoints already contained in B. There are no other
integer bases. In fact the body equals the convex hull of its
mixed source.

The total mass is M=2+a. Each of a,1,1 is strictly below M/2.
Moreover b=1>=s_d and |b-c|=0<a. Convexity of the d-th power gives

    s_d=((a^(1/d)+1)/2)^d <= (a+1)/2=s.               (5)

## 2. An explicit coupling satisfying the sharp density bound

Map A to C by

    T(x_1,x')=(k+(x_1-k)/a,x').

This positive diagonal affine map sends the uniform law on A to
the uniform law on C. Its midpoint map sends the uniform law on
A to the uniform law on D. Therefore the mass-a midpoint measure
is exactly

    eta=(a/s)1_D dx=(2a/(1+a))1_D dx
        <= (a/s_d)1_B dx.                            (6)

The actual support condition and the density bound are both proved
geometrically; eta is not an arbitrary hypothetical subdensity.
In d=1, s=s_d, so this attains the sharp density capacity exactly.

Because L=(1+a)/a, equation (6) gives L eta=2 1_D dx. The point (1)
has coordinates

    g=(g_a,1/2,...,1/2),
    g_a=(5+2a-a^2)/(4(2+a)).                           (7)

This follows from the first moment
1/2+(1+a)k, divided by total mass 2+a. The candidate is an actual
point of the middle fiber.

Every probability coupling of the same uniform marginals has
midpoint mean (g_A+g_C)/2=(k,1/2,...,1/2). Hence the point (7) is
independent of the coupling chosen. Changing the coupling cannot
repair the actual candidate failure proved below. In d=1, any
midpoint measure with the sharp bound in (6) is necessarily uniform
on D, since its support has volume s_d and it has mass a.

## 3. One actual oblique cap and its exact cost

Since (1-a)/2<g_a<1, the continuous halfspace H0={x_1>=g_a}
has the source cost

    |B intersect H0|+eta(H0)
       =(1-g_a)(1+2a/(1+a)).                          (8)

Now retain one actual ambient halfspace

    H={(z,x): x_1-z>=g_a}.                            (9)

It passes through (0,g). On base -1 its threshold is g_a-1<0,
so A is strictly fully captured. On base +1 its threshold is
g_a+1, strictly above max C=(5-a)/4. Indeed

    g_a-(1-a)/4=(3+3a)/(4(2+a))>0.

Thus C is strictly excluded. Its true mixed mass and normalized
mass are exactly

    mu(H)=1-g_a+a,
    mu(H)/M=(5a^2+10a+3)/(4(2+a)^2).                 (10)

All endpoint full/empty assertions are strict; no boundary atom or
supporting-face convention produces the counterexample. Only the
middle fiber is properly cut, with a null boundary.

For the specific coupling (6), the unpaired part of C contributes
zero to (9), and the midpoint pairing slack is exactly

    a-eta(H0)=a-(2a/(1+a))(1-g_a)>0.                  (11)

Adding this actual slack to (8) gives (10). Thus the deficit can
persist even after restoring all the actual endpoint payment;
it is not solely an artifact of discarding the pairing slack.

## 4. Sharp-capacity interval certificate

Take d=1 and a=1/10. The fibers are exactly

    A=[27/40,31/40], B=[0,1], C=[9/40,49/40].

Here s=s_1=11/20, eta=(2/11)1_[9/20,1], L=11 and
g_a=173/280. The proposed inequality (2) fails by the rational gap

    Gamma_1 M/2=21/40,
    |B intersect H0|+eta(H0)=1391/3080,
    21/40-1391/3080=113/1540>0.                       (12)

The actual oblique cap (9) has

    mu(H)=27/56,
    Gamma_1 M/2-mu(H)=3/70>0.                        (13)

The actual restored pairing slack is 47/1540. Thus even the sharp
density coefficient, all nonheavy inequalities, and the correct
full target mass in (1) do not make this candidate valid.

## 5. Positive full-volume planar certificate

Take d=2, a=1/100 and Q=[0,1]. This is a full three-dimensional
ambient body with three full planar rectangular fibers. Now

    s_2=121/400, s=101/200,
    eta density=2/101 < a/s_2=4/121,
    g_a=16733/26800.

The actual cap (9) has

    mu(H)=2067/5360,
    mu(H)/M=3445/17956 < 2/9=Gamma_2/2,
    2/9-3445/17956=4907/161604>0.                    (14)

Equation (8) is smaller still, so (2) also fails. This uses a
genuinely geometrically realized coupling satisfying the requested
dimensional bound, rather than an unconstrained density example.

The formula (10) tends to 3/16 as a tends to zero. This is an exact
parameterized cap formula, not an assertion of candidate failure
in every continuous dimension; the two claimed dimensions are
certified above.

## 6. A separate safe point and exact scope

At y=(0,1/2,...,1/2), retain the whole middle box B, the endpoint A
and its reflection (1-A_1) x Q in C. The latter inclusion is exact:

    1-A_1=[(1-a)/4,(1+3a)/4] subset C_1.

These three retained fibers form a centrally symmetric mixed
measure about y, with total mass 1+2a. Their midpoint interval is
[(1-a)/2,(1+a)/2], contained in B, so their lifted convex hull is
also an actual convex subbody of the original source. Every closed
halfspace through y retains at least half this mass. Consequently

    depth_mu(y)>=(1+2a)/(2(2+a))>1/4>=Gamma_d/2.       (15)

The specific bounds are 2/7 in the interval example and 17/67 in
the planar example. Thus the actual OC objective is safe here.

What fails is the precise proposed full-target midpoint-density
centroid bridge, including its version where one tries to repair
the candidate by selecting another uniform-marginal coupling.
The sharp coupling theorem itself and the already proved equal-
endpoint results are unchanged. A different candidate selection
or a genuinely stronger coupled geometry argument remains a
separate task.
